scope: Factual poll provenance check only; no vote-intention inference or probability change.
finding: The roughly three-quarters secondary claim concerns who prevailed in the Oct8 debate, not a candidate vote-intention estimate. AOL publisher syndication of Free Press text calls the online question totally unscientific. Detailed participation mechanics and the original WOOD poll remain unknown. No new representative vote-intention sample, fieldwork or topline was identified in this bounded source set.

free_press_poll.page_title: Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers U.S. Senate debate: Who won? Take our poll.
free_press_poll.date: 2026-10-08 23:10 UTC (AOL-reproduced Detroit Free Press page metadata)
free_press_poll.method_and_prompt: AOL reproduction of Free Press Opinion Staff text asks who won and calls the poll ‘totally unscientific’; no probability sample, voter screen, field dates, or poll sample size is stated. It links to the original Freep page.
free_press_poll.original_access: Direct Freep GET returned HTTP 402/paywall/challenge bytes; AOL full syndication page returned HTTP 200 and reproduces the text. Do not treat AOL as the Freep poll-results database.

wood_tv_and_summary_claim.claim: Common Dreams says the Detroit Free Press and WOOD-TV polls each showed about three-quarters believing El-Sayed prevailed. Its poll link points to a Yahoo-hosted video/article titled ‘Trump claims “jihadist lunatic” lost Michigan Senate debate. What do the polls say?’ The click-through returned HTTP 429 in browser; exact linked story body and underlying WOOD poll page/design were not recovered.
wood_tv_and_summary_claim.limits: Common Dreams provides no sample size, participant recruitment, field dates, weighting, uncertainty, or vote-intention figures for either debate-winner poll. WOOD poll's exact original page, method, and result remain unverified here.

source_summary: Freep original402; AOL licensed syndication200 attributes Free Press Opinion Staff, dates Oct8 23:10UTC, links the exact original and labels the debate-winner question totally unscientific. This supports an online impression question, not a representative candidate-support estimate. Self-selection is plausible but recruitment mechanics were not verified. CommonDreams Oct9 supplies a secondary WOOD characterization; exact WOOD body/design/result remain unverified. No odds or prices used.

collector_identity_erratum.cause: Collector copied another case market ID while retaining the correct MI condition ID. Root rejected the inconsistent identity before publication; no financial action or valuation relied on it.

primary_method_review: Root checked all four receipt/gzip/raw hashes and independently read the actual AOL attribution, original link, date and unscientific-method passage. Neither the secondary roughly75% claim nor an assumed sampling design was adopted as a new electoral estimate. These Oct8/9 items predate the IA Oct9–10 fieldwork already in the MI model.
